newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Main body of China troops enter Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Main body of China troops enter Hong Kong.

text.p: The main body of China's 4,000 troops who will defend Hong Kong streamed into the region in armoured cars, in trucks and by ship at dawn on the first day of Beijing rule.

The first soldiers of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) saluted from armoured personnel carriers and stood erect and stern in hundreds of open trucks as they crossed the line that divides China from its new Special Administrative Region at three border points.

Stone-faced in the open trucks under driving rain, the soldiers saluted cheering crowds welcoming them into Hong Kong and tens of thousands more who lined the streets of the booming Chinese border town of Shenzhen to watch them leave.

Hong Kong residents, braving the pouring rain or sheltering under umbrellas, placed garlands of flowers around the neck of Major-General Liu Zhenwu, commander of China's garrison in Hong Kong, as he arrived in the special region, television showed.
Local officials in Hong Kong presented Liu with a plaque reading: "Mighty and Civilised Troops".

The troops first snaked in a convoy of hundreds of vehicles through Shenzhen's streets, driving past a huge billboard from which the smiling figure of the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping looks down on the boomtown created by his daring reforms.
A navy patrol boat steamed out earlier from a Shenzhen wharf and was set to enter Hong Kong waters at 6 a.m., a ship's officer told state television.
The 10 naval vessels in the garrison were entering from the west in two formations and sail to Stonecutters Island.
The garrison used three main land crossing routes into Hong Kong and entered in 21 armoured cars and more than 400 other vehicles including army-green trucks, land cruisers and buses.
Helicopters due to take off from the Nantou airport in Shenzhen were delayed by the heavy rain, state television said.
The entry of the main contingent brings the size of the Chinese force in Hong Kong to nearly 5,000 after 509 troops entered late on Monday to reinforce 200 advance soldiers already in the territory.

The troops swiftly took over the barracks vacated just hours earlier by British soldiers who had defended the enclave for 156 years as a British colony. Britain handed over sovereignty to China at midnight on Monday.
